newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spain Feb CPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spain Feb CPI data.

text.p: The following is a selection of economists and analysts initial reaction to Spain's February Consumer Price Index, which fell 0.1 percent from January for a 2.5 percent rise year on year, versus 2.9 percent in January.
CARMEN HERNANSANZ, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH ESPANA

"This is a surprisingly good CPI. It's good in terms of practically all the components, except in services. There's a high probability that the Bank of Spain will cut rates by 25 basis points at tomorrow's repo or at the next one. In any case, we think that, there'll be a cut in March. Inflation data for the last two months gives sufficient room for it"
COLIN WARREN, ECONOMIST AT TOKAI BANK LONDON
"Both headline and core inflation fell very impressively, but service inflation is still stubborn (up 0.4 percent versus January) and this is what is worrying the Bank of Spain.

CPI declined so much mainly due to the fall in processed food, which is due, I suppose, to the olive oil fall. But I do not think the Bank of Spain --which has in mind its 1998 inflation target-- would cut rates on the basis of that fall.
In terms of the rate outlook, I guess they're still worried about service inflation.
The labour reform isn't ready yet. They will wait to see the peseta more stable and they would like to have more deficit numbers."
BELEN MATEOS, ECONOMIST AT ANALISTAS FINANCIEROS

"These are very good data, with CPI falling more than expected. Above all I'd highlight the fall in underlying inflation year on year to 2.3 percent. At first glance, the main reason seems to be processed foods. We wouldn't be surprised to see inflation fall even further in the next few months. The data shows the Bank of Spain has room to cut rates at Friday's repo."
RICCARDO BARBIERI, ECONOMIST AT MORGAN STANLEY LONDON
"I didn't expect such a good performance in Spain's inflation. After this February data it's very likely inflation this year can stay below 2.5 percent on average.
So it's now very likely that the Bank of Spain could cut its (six percent) key money market rate by at least 25 basis points, if not more."
VALENTIN FERNANDEZ, ECONOMIST AT CREDIT LYONNAIS ESPANA
"The data is great in almost all the components. Tomorrow the Bank of Spain will cut its key money rate 25 basis points"

"It's a relatively good figure, below forecasts, but the only problem is that February was the last month of a favourable cycle, as from next month the comparative data (from last year) will be very low. The market's response has been lukewarm. As regards tomorrow's (repo) auction, I'm a bit dubious. The bank of Spain could give a signal and cut rates by a quarter of a point, but I see a 60-40 chance that it won't."
